author: NicodemusArcleon
body:
> Is it possible to play without having to hunt for locations?

Yes. I play Aethric and the locations of dungeons are set. Same with towers. The only things you'll really have to "hunt" for are the memories. However, the map is set, and you can easily find them by just following the road. 

> Does the game have depth? Can you play it for about 2 years without getting bored?

Everything that exists in Orna (with a couple of small outliers) is in Aethric. I have been playing Orna and Aethric for over two years, and Aethric is my #1 played game. I don't play Orna as much anymore, since I stopped travelling for work.  As far as getting bored, endgame grind is endgame grind. But, there are so many updates to the game and the events, that there is always something to strive for.

author: lunar_heaven
body: From what I remember trying it out it's the same game with the same events but you control your character with an on screen d-pad. Different zones you can unlock and fast travel points to find so you're not having to walk to get back to places. There are locations you can get into with shops and bestiary and whatnot. Didn't get too far into it to say about the late game but like I mentioned it has the same game progression as the GPS variant.

author: petr1petr
body:
next to no difference.

even in ORNA (GPS version), you dont really have to move around - wayvessels allow you to travel to different places - so instead of going around your town, searching for something, you can just ask others, if they have wayvessel near that something. 

for some content, you should move, but if you dont want to, you dont have to (amities, settlements)

depth? yes, I am in for over 6 years and I am still having fun - and I am no exception - if you like it, it is for years. Besides, if you dont know too much about the game and if you dont get carry, it will take you quite a while to lvl up to 250.
